items.title: What is TPRS Glass known for in the glass processing industry?
items.content: TPRS Glass is a leading glass processing company in India, specializing in toughened glass, heat-strengthened glass, laminated glass, Curved glass, and architectural glazing solutions.

items.title: What does the brand TPRS Tuffsafe represent?
items.content: TPRS Tuffsafe is one of the key solutions offered by TPRS Glass, specializing in high-performance toughened and heat-strengthened safety glass designed for both residential and commercial applications.

items.title: Where is TPRS Glass located?
items.content: TPRS Glass operates from India, serving clients across 20+ countries with customized toughened glass solutions and advanced glass processing services.

items.title: What industries does TPRS Glass serve?
items.content: TPRS Glass serves the Architectural, Automotive, Locomotive, Vertical Mobility, Earthmovers, Refrigeration, and industrial sectors with durable and aesthetic glass solutions.

items.title: What makes TPRS Tuffsafe glass different from ordinary glass?
items.content: TPRS Tuffsafe glass undergoes controlled heat treatment, making it 4–5 times stronger than normal glass and highly resistant to thermal stress and impact.

items.title: What is toughened glass?
items.content: Toughened glass (also known as tempered glass) is a type of safety glass processed by controlled thermal treatments to increase strength and resistance.

items.title: What is heat-strengthened glass?
items.content: Heat-strengthened glass (HS glass) is produced by heating and slowly cooling glass to increase its strength, making it about twice as strong as annealed glass while retaining good clarity.

items.title: What happens if toughened glass breaks?
items.content: When broken, it shatters into small, blunt pieces, minimizing injury risk, a key safety advantage of TPRS Tuffsafe glass.

items.title: How does TPRS ensure glass quality?
items.content: TPRS Glass uses automated tempering furnaces, strict quality inspections, and in-house testing labs to maintain consistency.

items.title: Can toughened glass be cut after tempering?
items.content: No. Toughened glass cannot be cut or drilled after the tempering process. All processing must be done beforehand.

items.title: What is the edge quality of TPRS Tuffsafe glass?
items.content: TPRS offers polished, beveled, and seamed edges for enhanced finish and safety.

items.title: Does TPRS Tuffsafe glass support ceramic printing?
items.content: Yes, TPRS Tuffsafe glass supports ceramic frit printing for permanent design and branding.

items.title: Can toughened glass be laminated?
items.content: Yes, TPRS Lamisafe can combine two toughened sheets with PVB, EVA or SGP interlayers for extra protection.

items.title: How to clean toughened glass?
items.content: Use a soft cloth and mild glass cleaner; avoid abrasive materials.

items.title: What is TPRS Lamisafe?
items.content: TPRS Lamisafe is a laminated safety glass solution by TPRS Glass, engineered for enhanced strength, safety, and aesthetic appeal.

items.title: How does TPRS Lamisafe differ from normal glass?
items.content: Unlike standard glass, Lamisafe consists of two or more glass layers bonded with PVB, EVA, or SGP interlayers, providing impact resistance and shatter protection.

items.title: What certifications does TPRS Lamisafe glass meet?
items.content: TPRS Lamisafe complies with IS 2553 Part 1 & 2, CE, E-Mark, DOT, and QNL standards for safety, quality, and performance.

items.title: What are the available dimensions for TPRS Lamisafe glass?
items.content: Minimum: 300 mm x 450 mm, Maximum: 2300 mm x 4700 mm.

items.title: What process is used to process TPRS Lamisafe glass?
items.content: TPRS Lamisafe glass is horizontally nip-rolled or vacuum-processed, followed by controlled autoclaving for precision bonding.

items.title: What makes laminated glass a safety glass?
items.content: Its interlayer holds fragments together during breakage, ensuring protection and durability.

items.title: Does TPRS Lamisafe offer sound insulation?
items.content: Yes, it offers excellent acoustic performance, reducing outside noise effectively.

items.title: Can TPRS Lamisafe glass block UV rays?
items.content: Yes, laminated interlayers can block up to 99% of harmful UV radiation.

items.title: Is TPRS Lamisafe suitable for high-humidity or outdoor environments?
items.content: Yes, EVA and SGP laminated glass provide superior edge stability and moisture resistance.

items.title: What is Mesh Lamination?
items.content: Mesh Lamination integrates metal or fabric mesh between glass layers for unique aesthetics and added functionality.

items.title: What is Step Lamination?
items.content: Step Lamination provides seamless coverage while allowing flexibility for openings, overlaps, and stepped edges.

items.title: What is TPRS Wizardglass?
items.content: TPRS Wizardglass is a smart laminated glass that switches instantly between transparency and privacy using PDLC films.

items.title: What is Printed Lamination?
items.content: Printed Lamination combines durability with decorative or functional designs, ideal for interiors and façades.

items.title: What is Laminated DGU?
items.content: Laminated Double-Glazed Units (DGU) provide superior sound insulation, energy efficiency, and weather resistance.

items.title: Can Lamisafe glass include embedded materials?
items.content: Yes, it can incorporate fabrics, mesh, LEDs, and PDLC films within layers.

items.title: Is laminated glass used in automobiles?
items.content: Yes, TPRS Lamisafe curved laminated glass is used in windshields.

items.title: Is laminated glass suitable for skylights or canopies?
items.content: Yes, TPRS Lamisafe laminated glass ensures safety overhead and reduces glare.

items.title: Is TPRS Lamisafe glass suitable for sound studios or offices?
items.content: Yes, acoustic laminated glass reduces ambient and traffic noise efficiently.

items.title: How long does laminated glass last?
items.content: With proper installation, TPRS Lamisafe glass offers decades of performance with minimal degradation.

items.title: Is laminated glass weather-resistant?
items.content: Yes, it withstands heat, humidity, and UV exposure without delamination.

items.title: Can TPRS Lamisafe be curved or bent?
items.content: Yes, available as curved laminated glass for specialized applications.

items.title: What is the role of autoclaving in lamination?
items.content: It ensures complete bonding and removes air bubbles between layers for perfect clarity.

items.title: Which standards does TPRS Lamisafe follow?
items.content: IS 2553 (Part 1 & 2), CE, E-Mark, DOT, and QNL certifications.

items.title: What is TPRS Innovink?
items.content: TPRS Innovink is an advanced glass printing technology that combines ceramic digital printing, ceramic screen printing, UV printing, and lacquer coating for both functional and decorative applications.

items.title: What makes TPRS Innovink unique?
items.content: It fuses photorealistic design, energy efficiency, and lasting durability by embedding ceramic inks into glass at temperatures up to 700 °C, creating permanent and vibrant surfaces.

items.title: What equipment is used in TPRS Innovink printing?
items.content: TPRS Innovink uses DIP-TECH GPI Series printers with high-performance ceramic ink systems, ensuring world-class precision, color depth, and durability.

items.title: What is the difference between ceramic and UV printing?
items.content: Ceramic printing uses heat‑fused inks that create a durable, weather-resistant finish suitable for long-term use. UV printing delivers vivid colour and a smooth finish, making it best suited for visually rich indoor applications.

items.title: What is TPRS Innovink Lacquered Glass?
items.content: Back-painted glass with a sleek finish for wardrobes, wall panels, and kitchens.

items.title: Is the glass toughened before or after printing?
items.content: • Ceramic printing: Printed → then toughened. • UV printing: Toughened → then printed.

items.title: Can TPRS Innovink glass be laminated or insulated?
items.content: Yes, available as printed laminated, insulated, or heat-strengthened glass.

items.title: Can multi-layer printing be achieved?
items.content: Yes, enables gradients, depth, and shading effects.

items.title: Can frosted looks be created with TPRS Innovink?
items.content: Yes, digital or screen methods can simulate etched/frosted effects.

items.title: Can corporate logos be printed?
items.content: Yes, perfect for brand walls and storefronts.

items.title: Are metallic or gradient effects possible?
items.content: Yes, achieved through multi-layer ceramic printing.

items.title: Can one-way vision designs be achieved?
items.content: Yes, custom patterns enable privacy with light control.

items.title: How does TPRS Innovink save energy?
items.content: Printed patterns reduce solar heat gain and cooling loads.

items.title: Does it resist UV damage?
items.content: Yes, ceramic inks are UV-stable and fade-resistant.

items.title: Can TPRS Innovink prevent bird collisions?
items.content: Yes, patterned prints act as bird-safe glazing.

items.title: How long does the print last?
items.content: The ceramic layer lasts for the entire lifetime of the glass.

items.title: Where is TPRS Innovink Aura (UV Printing) best used?
items.content: For vivid interior applications like wall panels and decorative glass.

items.title: Can it be used in wet areas?
items.content: Yes, especially lacquered or UV-printed glass with edge sealing.

items.title: Is TPRS Innovink suitable for exterior façades?
items.content: Yes, ceramic-printed glass is fully weather-resistant.

items.title: What is TPRS Ecosafe Glass?
items.content: TPRS Ecosafe Glass is a high-performance insulated glass unit (IGU) engineered for superior thermal insulation, energy efficiency, and acoustic comfort in high-rise buildings and modern façades.

items.title: Who manufactures TPRS Ecosafe Glass?
items.content: It is exclusively processed by TPRS Glass, the only processor in India to hold Dowsil Quality Bond certification for both Insulating Glazing and Structural Glazing, ensuring international‑grade sealing and durability.​

items.title: What is the purpose of TPRS Ecosafe Glass?
items.content: To provide thermal insulation, energy savings, and soundproofing for commercial, residential, and institutional buildings.

items.title: How is TPRS Ecosafe Glass made?
items.content: Each unit has two or more glass panes separated by a spacer filled with desiccant and sealed using Butyl (primary) and Silicone (secondary) sealants.

items.title: How does TPRS Ecosafe Glass improve energy efficiency?
items.content: It reflects external heat while maintaining internal temperature balance, reducing HVAC load and overall energy consumption.

items.title: How much energy can TPRS Ecosafe Glass save?
items.content: Buildings may achieve 30–40 % lower cooling energy use, depending on configuration and building orientation.

items.title: How does TPRS Ecosafe Glass reduce heat gain?
items.content: Its low-E or solar-control coatings reflect infrared radiation, keeping interiors cooler during summer.

items.title: How does TPRS Ecosafe Glass minimize heat loss in winter?
items.content: The argon-gas or air cavity acts as a barrier, reducing interior heat escape.

items.title: Why is Argon gas used in TPRS Ecosafe IGUs?
items.content: Argon gas has 30 % lower thermal conductivity than air, offering better insulation and improved energy efficiency.

items.title: What percentage of Argon gas is used?
items.content: In select TPRS Ecosafe units, 90 % or more Argon is filled between panes for optimal thermal performance.

items.title: What glass types are available in TPRS Ecosafe IGUs?
items.content: Choices include clear, extra-clear, tinted, solar-control coated, and low-E coated glass.

items.title: What are the size limits for TPRS Ecosafe Glass?
items.content: Minimum – 300 mm × 300 mm; Maximum – 2500 mm × 4000 mm.

items.title: Is Argon gas safe?
items.content: Yes. It’s inert, non-toxic, colorless, and odorless, safe for all architectural and refrigeration applications.

items.title: What spacer materials are used?
items.content: Warm-edge aluminum or composite spacers with desiccant to absorb moisture and prevent fogging.

items.title: What sealants are applied?
items.content: Primary – Butyl; Secondary – Structural Silicone, both Dowsil Quality Bond certified.

items.title: What are the main benefits of TPRS Ecosafe Glass?
items.content: Enhanced insulation, energy efficiency, condensation resistance, noise reduction, and long-term durability.

items.title: How does TPRS Ecosafe Glass optimize daylight?
items.content: It allows abundant natural light while controlling glare and solar heat.

items.title: Where can TPRS Ecosafe Insulated Glass be used?
items.content: In façades, curtain walls, windows, skylights, hospitals, schools, airports, and premium vehicles.

items.title: Why is TPRS Ecosafe Glass used in hospitals and institutions?
items.content: It ensures temperature stability, quiet interiors, and patient comfort.

items.title: Why is TPRS Ecosafe Glass ideal for airports?
items.content: It offers thermal comfort, noise insulation, and optical clarity for terminals and control towers.

items.title: What is TPRS Archsafe Glass?
items.content: TPRS Archsafe Glass is precision-bent glass produced through controlled heating and molding, delivering elegant curves for Architectural Façades, Automotive Windshields, Aquariums, and White Goods Applications.

items.title: What makes TPRS Archsafe Glass different from ordinary glass?
items.content: Unlike flat glass, TPRS Archsafe Glass is thermoformed into curves, providing greater aesthetic appeal, structural integrity, and optical clarity.

items.title: What industries use TPRS Archsafe Glass?
items.content: It’s used in Architecture, Automotive, Aquariums, and Home Appliances such as Refrigerators, Displays, and Chimneys.

items.title: How is TPRS Archsafe Glass made?
items.content: Flat glass is heated to a high temperature and formed over precision-engineered Die to achieve smooth, accurate curvature.

items.title: Where is TPRS Archsafe Glass used in architecture?
items.content: In office façades, windows, skylights, canopies, staircases, and balustrades for modern, seamless design.

items.title: What is Wizardglass (Switchable Glass)?
items.content: Wizardglass is TPRS's innovative switchable glass technology using Polymer Dispersed Liquid Crystal (PDLC) that allows instant control over transparency. The glass switches from clear to opaque with electrical activation, providing on-demand privacy and light control.

items.title: How does TPRS Wizardglass work?
items.content: When an electric current (35–70 VAC) passes through the PDLC film, the liquid crystals align, making the glass transparent. When switched off, the crystals scatter light, turning the glass opaque.

items.title: What is the difference between PDLC laminated glass and retrofit film?
items.content: Laminated glass integrates the PDLC film between two glass layers during manufacturing, offering durability and safety. Retrofit uses a film sticker applied on existing glass, suitable for quick upgrades.

items.title: What are the available size ranges?
items.content: Minimum: 200 mm × 200 mmMaximum: 1900 mm × 3700 mm

items.title: What voltage does it require to operate?
items.content: It operates on a low-voltage AC supply of 35–70 VAC via a dedicated controller.

items.title: What are TPRS Winsafe window frames?
items.content: TPRS Winsafe window frames are precision-engineered aluminium frames designed for buses and trains, offering strength, durability, and smooth operation.

items.title: What materials are used in TPRS Winsafe window frames?
items.content: We use high-grade aluminium profiles, EPDM rubber sealing, precision-machined components, and high-quality glazing materials.

items.title: What is the maximum size available for your window frames?
items.content: The maximum manufacturing size is 1311 mm x 1418 mm.

items.title: Do you provide sliding window frames for buses and trains?
items.content: Yes, we offer smooth operable sliding frames with precise fabrication and EPDM sealing for easy operation and long-term performance.

items.title: Do you manufacture window frames for AC buses?
items.content: Yes. We offer AC-compatible framed windows engineered to support insulation and reduced air leakage.

items.title: Why choose TPRS Glass for façade and curtain wall solutions?
items.content: TPRS Glass have proven expertise in large-scale execution, precision fabrication, use of high-performance glass, and a track record with top clients like airports and IT parks.

items.title: What is a building façade?
items.content: A façade is the exterior face or front of a building, often made of glass, metal, or stone, designed for aesthetic appeal and natural light entry.

items.title: What materials does TPRS use for modern façades?
items.content: Toughened glass, laminated glass, DGU, Low-E glass, and switchable glass, depending on design and performance needs.

items.title: What is the purpose of architectural glass in façades?
items.content: It enhances appearance, ensures energy efficiency, offers acoustic comfort, and controls UV and solar gain.

items.title: What are glass fins?
items.content: Long vertical glass strips mounted perpendicular to façades, used for decoration, shading, or structural stiffening.

items.title: Where is glass used in buses?
items.content: Glass is used in the Windshield, Side Windows, Rear Glass, Roof/Skylight Glass, Entry and Exit Doors, Emergency Exit Windows, and Digital Glass Displays.

items.title: What are the main glass components in a bus?
items.content: Key components include the Front Windshield, Side Windows, Rear Glass, Door Glass, Roof Skylights, and Emergency Exit Glass Panels.

items.title: What makes TPRS Glass a unique solution in the automobile industry?
items.content: TPRS Glass offers end-to-end in-house facilities, including toughening, lamination, precision bent glass and ceramic printing, ensuring superior durability, clarity, and reliability.

items.title: What is the standard glass used for the bus windshield?
items.content: Laminated glass is used for windshields to ensure safety, sound insulation, and clear visibility.

items.title: What is the tint percentage in bus windshields and windows?
items.content: Windshields typically have 70% visible light transmission, while side windows have around 50% for privacy and glare reduction.

items.title: Where is glass used in earthmoving equipment?
items.content: Primarily in Driver/Operator Cabins, including Windshields, Side Windows, Rear Glass, and Door Panels.

items.title: Which machines fall under the Earthmover segment?
items.content: Excavators, Bulldozers, Dump Trucks, Backhoes, Loaders, Graders, Compactors, and Scrapers.

items.title: Why is glass essential in earthmovers?
items.content: It ensures visibility, operator safety, weather protection, and improves comfort inside the cabin.

items.title: What is TPRS’s specialization in the earthmover sector?
items.content: TPRS specializes in defogger windshields, rear defogger glass, laminated bend glass (L-shaped), sash windows, glass-in-glass assemblies, and toughened safety glass.

items.title: Where can TPRS Glass be used in earthmoving equipment?
items.content: In construction, mining, airport ground support, agriculture, and infrastructure sectors.

items.title: What is the role of glass in LED lighting systems?
items.content: Glass plays a vital role in LED lighting by providing light diffusion, clarity, and protection. TPRS Glass processes precision toughened glass that enhances brightness and ensures uniform light distribution in LED fixtures.

items.title: How does glass maintain its finish over time in switch boards?
items.content: TPRS Glass remains scratch-free and glossy even after long-term use, unlike traditional plastic panels.

items.title: Why is glass preferred over plastic in high-temperature lighting?
items.content: Unlike plastic, TPRS Glass can endure extreme heat without warping or discoloration, ensuring consistent performance.

items.title: How does toughened glass improve electrical panel safety?
items.content: TPRS Tuffsafe - Toughened Glass provides superior insulation, preventing shocks and protecting internal circuits from heat.

items.title: What are the advantages of using back-painted (lacquered) glass in switches?
items.content: TPRS Glass offers rich, customizable colors through back-painting, enhancing design flexibility and luxury aesthetics.

items.title: What is TPRS’s role in the locomotive sector?
items.content: TPRS processes high-performance safety and specialty glass solutions for trains, metros, and locomotives, ensuring durability, comfort, and aesthetics.

items.title: What are TPRS’s specializations in locomotive glass?
items.content: TPRS specializes in Driver and Passenger Windows, Door Glass, Emergency Exit Glass, Train Windshields, Switchable Glass, DGU with Blinds, Cabin Mirrors, and Nosecone Windshields.

items.title: Where is glass used in trains and locomotives?
items.content: In driver windshields, passenger windows, AC coach doors, emergency exits, destination boards, roof panels, and interior partitions.

items.title: What type of glass is used for train windshields?
items.content: TPRS Lamisafe laminated glass provides high impact resistance and optical clarity.

items.title: Why is laminated glass preferred for train windshields?
items.content: It ensures safety against flying debris, maintains visibility under impact, and offers sound insulation.

items.title: What are TPRS’s specializations in the marine segment?
items.content: TPRS specializes in laminated glass with SentryGlas™ lonoplast interlayers, toughened safety glass, DGU (double-glazed) flat glass, and custom marine mirrors.

items.title: Where is TPRS glass used in marine applications?
items.content: TPRS Glass is used in Ship and Yacht Windows, Windshields, Roof Panels, Control Cabins, and Interior Mirrors. It ensures visibility, safety, insulation, and aesthetic appeal in demanding Marine environments.​

items.title: What are the main types of marine glass supplied by TPRS?
items.content: Laminated Glass (Sentry Interlayer), Toughened Glass, DGU Glass (Double‑Glazed), Flat Windows, Roof Glass, Mirrors, and Windshields.

items.title: Why choose TPRS for marine glass solutions?
items.content: TPRS provides custom‑engineered, Heat‑Treated, Laminated, and DGU Marine Glass that offers durability, clarity, and high-performance safety.

items.title: Why is laminated glass with a SentryGlas™ interlayer used in marine applications?
items.content: Because the SentryGlas™ interlayer interlayer provides superior strength, durability, and moisture resistance, making the glass ideal for high-humidity, high-wind, and marine environments.

items.title: What are TPRS’s specializations in the refrigeration industry?
items.content: TPRS specializes in energy-efficient, anti-fog glass systems such as TPRS Ecosafe (IGU doors), TPRS Tuffsafe (shelves), and TPRS Archsafe (curved deli glass).

items.title: Where is glass used in refrigeration equipment?
items.content: In display doors, freezer doors, glass canopies, interior shelves, and deli counter covers.

items.title: What are the main glass types TPRS supplies for refrigeration?
items.content: IGU (Insulated Glazing Units), Defogger Glass, Curved Glass, and Toughened Shelving Glass.

items.title: Why is glass important in refrigeration systems?
items.content: It ensures visibility, insulation, hygiene, and contributes to energy savings by maintaining temperature consistency.

items.title: What is the purpose of IGU glass in refrigeration?
items.content: It provides insulation, prevents condensation, and improves energy efficiency by maintaining low internal temperatures.

items.title: Which products does TPRS supply to the vertical mobility industry?
items.content: TPRS supplies Side and Balustrade Panels, Landing Panels, Cabin Glass, Doors, LOP/COP Panels, Mirrors, and Fire-Rated and Printed Decorative Glass.

items.title: What glass types are commonly used in escalators and elevators?
items.content: Toughened glass, Laminated glass, Printed glass, Fire-rated glass, Mesh/Fabric laminated glass, and Switchable glass.

items.title: Why is glass preferred in modern escalator and elevator design?
items.content: It offers a sleek, open, and contemporary aesthetic while ensuring safety, durability, and easy maintenance.

items.title: Where is glass used in escalators?
items.content: In side panels/balustrades, landing panels, and end panels to enhance safety and aesthetics.

items.title: What are balustrade panels?
items.content: Transparent or tinted side panels on escalators that provide protection while maintaining visibility and design appeal.

items.title: What is TPRS Glass role in the white goods industry?
items.content: TPRS Glass processes high-performance glass components that combine aesthetics, heat resistance, and durability for leading appliance brands.

items.title: Which TPRS brands serve the white goods sector?
items.content: Tuffsafe (toughened glass), Ecosafe (insulated energy-efficient glass), Archsafe (curved glass), and Innovink (printed glass).

items.title: Why is glass important in white goods?
items.content: It provides safety, functionality, transparency, and visual appeal while withstanding heat, pressure, and chemicals.

items.title: Where is glass used in ovens and OTGs?
items.content: In front doors, viewing windows, and inner panels to allow users to see food while insulating heat.

items.title: What type of glass is used for oven doors?
items.content: Tempered (toughened) glass capable of withstanding up to 300°C.
